implementation_notes: Scala accumulates layers through the language as well as libraries: Scala 2 collection idioms beside Scala 3 ones during a migration, Akka beside Cats/Future for concurrency, circe and Play JSON both used in a Play application. The Akka case is the clearest — a licence change and an ecosystem fragmentation made the 'migrate to something else' plan a decade-long project in exactly the pattern lava flow describes. The completion mechanism is a compiler flag (`-Xfatal-warnings` plus `-Wconf`) or a scalafix rule that fails the build on the legacy API, so the migration has a mechanism rather than an intention.
idiom_name: Akka and its own futures library; two JSON libraries; Scala 2 and 3 idioms
pitfalls: Two JSON libraries produce subtly different parsing and printing behaviour for the same case classes.
Scala 2 and 3 collection APIs differ in behaviour, not just syntax, so a half-migrated codebase has results that differ by file.
An Akka migration blocked by a transitive dependency can run indefinitely without anyone deciding to stop it.
